definition: The two inference phases: prefill processes the entire prompt in parallel (compute-bound, determines time to first token), decode generates tokens one by one (memory-bandwidth-bound, determines tokens per second).
details: The two inference phases: prefill processes the entire prompt in parallel (compute-bound, determines time to first token), decode generates tokens one by one (memory-bandwidth-bound, determines tokens per second). They stress hardware differently, motivating separate optimization and even separate hardware pools.

explainer.lead: LLM inference splits into prefill, which processes the whole prompt in parallel, and decode, which emits tokens one at a time. The split matters because each phase stresses hardware differently and sets different user-facing numbers.

tiers.eli5: Reading the whole question in one go is one job, and answering word by word is a separate job, and each is slow for different reasons.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers track prefill as compute-bound and gating time to first token, and decode as memory-bandwidth-bound and gating tokens per second. The pitfall is optimizing one phase while ignoring the other, which just moves the bottleneck.
tiers.paperLevel: Prefill processes the entire prompt in parallel; decode generates tokens one by one. Since they stress hardware differently, they motivate separate optimization and even separate hardware pools.

explainer.example: A long document prompt is handled in a single parallel prefill pass, then the summary streams out one token at a time during decode.
